true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition silently replaces the width/height API

Ruby does not overload methods. `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 is immediately replaced by `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149, so the first method is dead. Any existing caller that passes numeric max width and max height (the previous public signature) now hits the new method: the width is treated as an ImageMagick geometry string and the height integer is treated as `opts`. `opts[:allow_animation]` then raises, or the convert command is built with a bogus geometry, so thumbnail downsizing elsewhere breaks.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client size check hardcodes 10MB for every upload type

`validateUploadedFile` used to compare against `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so images and attachments had independent admin limits. It now always uses `10 * 1024`. Attachments are no longer limited by `max_attachment_size_kb` (users can upload up to 10MB, or are blocked at 10MB if the admin allowed more). The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcode and always reports a 10MB image limit, so the error text is wrong for attachments and for any site whose real cap is not 10MB.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
API URL downloads ignore the configured size cap for non-images

`FileHelper.download` used to stop at `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. It now always fetches up to `10.megabytes` for every API URL upload, including attachments. Only filenames that `FileHelper.is_image?` enter the new downsize loop, so a non-image fetched from a URL can be stored at up to 10MB even when `max_attachment_size_kb` (or `max_image_size_kb`) is much smaller. That is a server-side bypass of the site setting, not just a client check.

ImageMagick convert reads and writes the same tempfile path

The new downsize loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`. `convert` (and gifsicle) are invoked with the same path as input and output. ImageMagick truncates the destination before it finishes reading the source when they are the same file, so the upload can be corrupted or emptied. The loop then keeps resizing that damaged file, and `Upload.create_for` still stores whatever is left.

Oversized images are stored even when downsize fails or does not shrink enough

The loop ignores the boolean returned by `OptimizedImage.downsize` and, after at most five attempts, always continues to `Upload.create_for` with the current tempfile. If convert fails, the file does not get smaller (percentage plus the `\>` shrink-only geometry often will not), or five 80% passes are not enough, the image is persisted above `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. Combined with the client and `FileHelper.download` now allowing 10MB regardless of that setting, the configured image size limit is no longer enforced.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing host records raise instead of 404

update and destroy load the row with where(id:).first and then call save_host or destroy with no nil check. An unknown id makes host nil and raises NoMethodError (500) rather than a not-found response. save_host also assumes params[:embeddable_host] is present, so a body without that key 500s the same way.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Allowlist host compare is case-sensitive on the URL side

record_for_host sets host = uri.host and queries lower(host) = ? without downcasing the bound value. A referer or embed URL whose host differs only in case (EvilTrout.com vs stored eviltrout.com) does not match, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? denies a host that was saved and comments/import are rejected.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are inserted raw and unescaped

Existing embeddable_hosts values are interpolated into INSERT with '#{h}' and are not normalized. A host containing a quote breaks or injects SQL during upgrade. Values stored as 'http://example.com' or with a path (which the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? accepted) are saved verbatim, while EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? compares URI#host to the column, so previously working embeds stop matching after migration.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Category and embeddable-host fabricators were swapped

category_fabricator.rb now only defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), and the category, diff_category, happy_category, and private_category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Anything that loads fabricators by the category file, or a later cleanup that deletes the misnamed file, drops Fabricate(:category) and breaks the suite, including the new embed specs that depend on it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are inserted raw and unescaped

Existing embeddable_hosts values are interpolated into INSERT with '#{h}' and are not normalized. A host containing a quote breaks or injects SQL during upgrade. Values stored as 'http://example.com' or with a path (which the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? accepted) are saved verbatim, while EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? compares URI#host to the column, so previously working embeds stop matching after migration.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when embed_category is unset

The data migration always does execute(...)[0]['id'] on the embed_category join. If that site setting was never saved, or its value does not exactly match a category name, the query returns no row, [0] is nil, and the migration raises NoMethodError before the uncategorized_category_id fallback. Any upgrade that has not configured embed_category will fail while creating embeddable_hosts and will not reach the DELETE of the old settings.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

false_positives.candidate:
Plural _ids hydration assumes a non-null array

The new *_ids branch always calls obj[k].map. If a rest payload includes a key such as color_ids or embeddable_host_ids set to null (or any non-array), hydration throws and the whole find/findAll fails. This is a shared store path, not limited to embedding, so any serializer that emits a null has-many id list now breaks client loads.

PostCreator is given a category id as a name

Import now passes category: eh.try(:category_id). PostCreator's :category option is a category name (it looks up Category by name); the numeric id belongs in category_id. The lookup misses, so newly imported embed topics are not filed in the host's category and fall through to the default/uncategorized category. The per-host category feature this PR adds does not take effect on create.

embed: :ids cannot read ids from OpenStruct

has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids makes the serializer call embeddable_host_ids. Admin::EmbeddingController builds an OpenStruct with only id and embeddable_hosts, so that method is missing and returns nil via method_missing. The customize/embedding JSON therefore has no host ids to hydrate, and the admin UI loads with an empty host list even when rows exist.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser exists

unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(...) and then calls tu.notification_level with no nil check. Notification mail can be sent to a user who has no topic_users row (or the row can be missing for other reasons). Clicking the new per-topic link then raises NoMethodError and the user is not unsubscribed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct save skips reason flag, so mute does not stick

The new action assigns notification_level and calls tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change. That skips notifications_reason_id, notifications_changed_at, and the MessageBus notification_level_change publish. update_last_read auto-promotes to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and the user has viewed the topic long enough, so a mute from this link is undone the next time they read the topic, and other open clients never see the change.

Unsubscribe is a non-idempotent GET with no token

TopicsController#unsubscribe is a logged-in GET that immediately writes TopicUser.notification_level. Mail clients, link scanners, and prefetchers follow GET links, and another site can trigger it with the session cookie (CSRF). The update is also not idempotent: watching/tracking is set to regular, and a second request (refresh or a scanner plus the real click) then sets muted. Users can lose topic notifications without choosing to, or land on a different level than the first click intended.

Unsubscribe page claims success without unsubscribing

The Ember topicUnsubscribe route only loads the topic, clears notificationReasonText, and renders stopNotificiationsText ('You will stop receiving notifications...'). It never calls the server to change notification level. The message is an unescaped HTML claim of a side effect this route does not perform. In-app visits, or a server action that stops mutating on GET, show a false confirmation while the user remains subscribed until they happen to use the dropdown.

Watching users are not actually unsubscribed

If notification_level is above regular (tracking or watching — the people who receive topic emails), the action sets regular rather than muted. The email copy says this link stops notifications for the topic, but regular still delivers mentions, quotes, and replies-to-you. Only a second accidental request mutes them. The level change also does not match the Ember page, which tells the user they will stop receiving notifications.

unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url

server.en.yml unsubscribe_link always interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, and MessageBuilder appends I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) whenever add_unsubscribe_link is set. template_args only contains unsubscribe_url if the caller passed it. Any other mailer or plugin that sets add_unsubscribe_link without that option raises a missing-interpolation error and fails to send, or emits a broken link. There is no default, and List-Unsubscribe still points only at user preferences.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Block check writes stats non-atomically on every validation

should_block? increments match_count in memory and calls save as a side effect of validation, including for action_type :do_nothing. UsersController#create always calls user.valid? and then user.save, and each runs EmailValidator, so one signup attempt counts twice. The read-modify-write is also not atomic, so concurrent attempts lose increments. A failure in that save (lock, statement error) aborts registration instead of returning a normal email validation error.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Domain allow/deny regex is unanchored and under-escaped

email_in_restriction_setting? only backslash-escapes dots, then compiles /@(#{domains})/i and tests with =~. There is no end anchor, so a whitelist of "company.com" also matches "user@company.com.attacker.com" and the address is allowed. Other regex metacharacters in the site setting (+, *, parentheses, and so on) are interpolated raw, so a crafted or merely punctuation-heavy domain list can change what the check matches or raise RegexpError and fail signup.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Block list lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized

BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the address with an exact WHERE email = ? match, and EmailValidator passes the raw attribute through. Signup (User.new_from_params) never downcases or strips the address, and the unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive. A blocked row for "bad@spam.com" therefore does not match "Bad@spam.com" or "bad@spam.com ". Changing case is enough to skip the new block and still create the account.

false_positives.candidate:
Rejected-email cache is case-sensitive and mislabels the error

After a failed create, the submitted address is stored in rejectedEmails and later rejected with I18n.t('user.email.invalid'). contains() is case-sensitive, so editing only the case clears the client block and resubmits. The generic "invalid" string also hides the server's blocked/not-allowed reason, which is the only signal the new block list produces.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resize messages are accepted if origin is a substring of discourseUrl

The listener keeps a message when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1`. That is the reverse of an origin check and is not an equality comparison. Any event whose origin string appears inside the configured discourse URL is trusted, and `e.data.height` is written onto the iframe. A crafted postMessage from a matching substring origin can resize or distort the embed; a trailing-slash or path mismatch can also reject the real forum origin.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer, not an origin

The embed layout calls `parent.postMessage(..., request.referer)`. postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme, host, and optional port). A referer includes path and query, so browsers throw or drop the message. The parent frame in embed.js never receives `discourse-resize`, and the iframe height stays at the default.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Imported HTML is stored and shown unsanitized (stored XSS)

TopicEmbed.import appends the source URL into an HTML fragment with no escaping (`<a href='#{url}'>`), and the only check is that the string starts with http:// or https://. A URL such as `http://example.com/'><script>...` therefore becomes script in the post body. The same method stores RSS and Readability HTML as cook_method raw_html. Post#cook (app/models/post.rb:133) returns that raw string unchanged, skipping the normal renderer and sanitizer, and the embed view prints it with `raw`. PollFeed also passes feed item HTML straight through (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35). Anyone who can influence the feed, the remote page, or the embed URL can store script that runs for every forum user and inside the embed iframe.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embed template has invalid ERB and will not render

The header branch is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which is not valid Ruby/ERB (`end` cannot be followed by `if` like that). When a topic embed exists, EmbedController#best renders this template and ActionView will raise a syntax error, so the comments iframe never shows highlights. It should be `<% end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed poll crashes when an item has no content

`i.content.scrub` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a content string. Many feeds only set description or summary, so content is nil and this raises NoMethodError. Because the exception is inside `rss.items.each` and the job sets `retry: false`, one incomplete item aborts the whole hourly import and no later items are imported.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Any client with a spoofable referer can enqueue fetch jobs

best enqueues :retrieve_topic for every embed_url that is not already imported, with no host check, rate limit, or authentication in the request. The 60-second throttle lives inside the job after it has already been queued. A caller that sets Referer to the embeddable host can flood Sidekiq with retrieve jobs (and each miss may also run a full feed poll). The controller spec expects a synchronous TopicRetriever#retrieve, so this path is also untested and the new spec will fail.

Blank embed username crashes remote fetch

fetch_http does `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` with no presence check. PollFeed guards on embed_by_username, but EmbedController enqueues RetrieveTopic for any missing embed, and perform_retrieve calls fetch_http whenever the host is allowed. If the username setting is blank, the job raises NoMethodError on nil and the embed stays on the loading page.

Content hash is updated even when the revision fails

On a changed embed, import always calls `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` after `revise!`, without checking that revise! returned true or that the post saved. If validation, a missing post, or a rollback causes the update to fail, the stored hash still matches the new body, so later polls treat the topic as up to date and never retry the revision.

embed_url is limited to 255 characters

embed_url is a string column, which on this Rails/Postgres setup defaults to varchar(255), with a unique index on the full value. Article and feed URLs with long paths or query strings exceed that limit, so TopicEmbed.create! raises and the import is rolled back. Those pages can never be embedded or polled.

import_remote fetches arbitrary URLs with Kernel.open

import_remote calls `open(url).read` before any http(s) or host check. Ruby's Kernel.open treats a leading `|` as a shell command, and open-uri will follow redirects to internal addresses and file URLs. Disqus import passes `t[:link]` from the XML export straight into this method, and TopicRetriever only checks the initial host, not the redirect target. An untrusted Disqus file or an embeddable page that redirects can make the worker read local files, hit internal services, or run commands.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items() emits invalid and mismatched vendor properties

align-items() sets -webkit-box-align to the modern keyword unchanged, and also sets a non-existent -ms-align-items. The 2009 box model uses start/end/center/baseline/stretch, not flex-start/flex-end, and there is no -moz-box-align even though flexbox() sets display: -moz-box. -ms-flex-align is the only legacy align property that is real. Call sites that pass center or baseline happen to be legal for -webkit-box-align, but flex-start/flex-end (or any future caller) will be ignored by old WebKit while modern align-items still applies, so vertical alignment of the header, small-action rows, and bullet badges will differ across the browsers these prefixes are meant to cover.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() maps 0-based order onto 1-based box-ordinal-group

The new order mixin copies $val straight into -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (default 1); the standard order property is 0-based (default 0). The correct prefix is $val + 1. As written, an item with order(1) shares a group with unspecified siblings in old WebKit/Firefox, and order(0) is an invalid ordinal (dropped, so the item stays at the default). Header callers pass order(2) and order(3), which currently sort the same as modern order only by luck; any 0 or 1 value will reorder .panel / .extra-info-wrapper differently in prefixed engines than in current browsers.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

false_positives.candidate:
Action button float is ignored inside new flex container

.small-action is now a flex container (flexbox + align-items), but its button still uses float: right. Float does not apply to flex items, so the expand/details button stays in source order immediately after .small-action-desc instead of being pinned to the right edge. The old left padding (4em) that reserved space beside the floated avatar was also removed, so this row no longer matches the previous layout in any browser that honors display: flex. Use margin-left: auto on the button (and drop the floats) if the button is meant to sit at the end of the row.

Panel right-alignment depends on auto margin that 2009 flex ignores

.panel lost float: right and now relies on margin-left: auto plus order(3), while .contents is turned into a flex container via the new flexbox() mixin (display: -webkit-box / -moz-box / -ms-flexbox / flex). Auto margins do not absorb free space in the 2009 box model those prefixes enable, and floats on flex/box items are ignored, so there is no fallback. In engines that honor -webkit-box or -moz-box but not modern flex, the header panel (login, icons) will sit next to the title instead of on the right. .d-header .title { float: left } was removed in the same change, so the title no longer floats either when flex is absent.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is never used as the serializer predicate

ActiveModel Serializers only honors include hooks named include_<attr>?. This method is defined as include_website_name (no question mark), so it is dead code. website_name is therefore always emitted, including when website is blank or URI parsing fails and the method returns nil. The intended omission never happens.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-site check treats any hostname suffix as the forum domain

The else branch treats the site as the same domain whenever Discourse.current_hostname ends with '.' plus the website host. That is true for any suffix, not only a parent domain: a forum at forum.example.com will treat a website host of com (or example.com.evil is not the issue, but com and other intermediate suffixes are) as internal and append the path. A user website of http://com/user is therefore labeled com/user instead of com. The equal-label sibling check above has the same over-match for unrelated hosts that only share a tail (evil.example.com vs forum.example.com).

website_name bypasses the TL0 anonymous field restriction

website is listed in untrusted_attributes, so anonymous viewers of a trust-level-0 user do not receive the website. website_name is a new public attribute and is not included in that list, and nothing else checks scope.restrict_user_fields?. The profile template now renders model.website_name, so the host and path that used to stay hidden are sent to anonymous clients. Previously the client derived the label from model.website, which was absent in that case.

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embedded-post author color inverted instead of complemented

The embedded topic-meta author link used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement keeps the light-theme branch at 70% and the dark branch at 30%, so both themes get the opposite mute level from the rest of this change. On the default light theme the name becomes much lighter (worse contrast); on a dark theme it stays too close to the background instead of the intended scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%). It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

true_positives.golden_comment: This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Group member name mute level changed from 30% to 50%

.user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses 50% for both the $primary and $secondary branches, so light-theme names get lighter than before and dark-theme names are not lightened by the complementary 70%. The sibling .title rule in the same block was already 50% and was converted correctly; only .name was altered.

true_positives.golden_comment: In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Custom message length color arguments are swapped

.custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The new call uses 30% on the light branch and 70% on the dark branch, which is the reverse of the desktop modal (70% / 30%) and of the complement rule used everywhere else. Light themes therefore render this hint much darker than before, and dark themes lighten $secondary by 70% so the text is far less muted than the original 70% fade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.

The embedded topic-meta author link used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement keeps the light-theme branch at 70% and the dark branch at 30%, so both themes get the opposite mute level from the rest of this change. On the default light theme the name becomes much lighter (worse contrast); on a dark theme it stays too close to the background instead of the intended scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%). true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages is one too high when count divides evenly

totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (the default page size is 50, so 50, 100, … members), this reports an extra empty page. showingLast then stays false on the real last page, so Next is enabled and loads a blank page. Use ceil(user_count / limit), and keep the zero-count special case.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. true_positives.golden_comment: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Add/remove members read group_id but the route only sets id

add_members and remove_member both do Group.find(params.require(:group_id)). The routes added in config/routes.rb are member routes (DELETE/PUT /admin/groups/:id/members), so Rails supplies params[:id], not params[:group_id]. The client also only puts the group id in the path (/admin/groups/:id/members.json) and does not send a group_id field. ParameterMissing (or a failed lookup) means adding and removing members from the admin UI will 400. Controller specs pass only because they inject group_id directly and never exercise the route.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

false_positives.candidate:
Creating a group drops alias_level

create only assigns name and visible from params. The client asJSON() also sends alias_level, and the new-group form exposes the alias-level combo box before the group has an id. That value is ignored, so every new group is stored with the default alias level (nobody) regardless of what the admin selected. Update does honor alias_level, so the setting only sticks on a later save.

Member row template looks up fields on the wrong context

group.hbs renders members with the non-block helper {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}. In this Ember version the item view's context is the user, and the named `member` binding is not available inside the item template. The template still uses {{member.username}}, {{avatar member}}, and {{action "removeMember" member}}, so avatars/usernames will not render and remove will be invoked without a user. `automatic` is also read from that user context, so the guard that hides the remove control for automatic groups does not work.

Members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit and offset

limit and offset are taken straight from query params with no upper bound, no positive-only check, and no cap. Previously automatic groups were limited (default 200). Anyone who can see the group can now request an arbitrarily large page (or a negative offset, which PostgreSQL rejects). That can turn the public members list into a full dump and a cheap DoS. Clamp limit to a small maximum and reject negative offset/limit.

Removing a member bypasses Group#remove

remove_member deletes the user with group.users.delete(user_id), then calls group.save. The previous membership path used Group#remove, which is what add still uses (group.add). Association#delete skips Group#remove callbacks and any counter-cache, primary-group, or notification side effects that remove performs, so user_count and related state can stay stale after a successful admin removal.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Custom fallback list drops parent-locale fallbacks

Production previously set config.i18n.fallbacks = true, which used I18n::Locale::Fallbacks and walked parent tags (zh_TW -> zh -> default locale). FallbackLocaleList#[] now returns only [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]. Regional locales no longer fall back to their language root, so a missing zh_TW key will not use an existing zh translation and will jump straight to the site default or English. The same method also calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym with no guard; if that setting is nil or SiteSetting cannot be read (boot, asset precompile, DB outage), every I18n lookup raises instead of translating.

Fallback locale files are not loaded on the translation path

I18n.translate only calls load_locale for the active locale, and the new ensure_loaded! helper is never invoked from translate, with_locale, or reload. Fallback YAML is loaded only from ApplicationController#set_locale via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Sidekiq jobs, mailers, and any I18n.with_locale block therefore resolve fallbacks against unloaded site-default and :en files, so missing keys do not fall back to translations that exist on disk. No-argument lookups then freeze that miss in the LRU cache (key is only key+locale+backend), so a later load of the fallback locale still returns the wrong result until restart.

Translation cache ignores the fallback chain

The LRU key is "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}" and does not include SiteSetting.default_locale or the fallback list. FallbackLocaleList recomputes the chain on every lookup, but a cache hit never reaches the backend. After an admin changes the site default locale, strings that were filled from the old fallback stay pinned to the previous language for that user locale until the entry is evicted or the process reloads.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile

UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added on UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). There is no no-arg overload on this class or its parents, so this change does not compile and the re-authentication skip cannot be built or shipped. The intended call is almost certainly isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which is already non-null in this branch.

true_positives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Conditional passkeys UI only filled when a user is already set

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, and both authenticate() (around line 115) and the error challenge() override (around line 137) now use that helper to decide whether to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm. Previously fillContextForm ran whenever passkeys were enabled and the user was not yet selected — the conditional-UI / discoverable-credential login path. With the new check, the first username/password page (user still null) and invalid-credential re-renders that happen before context.setUser never receive challenge, rpId, or ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI. Re-authentication is covered, but ordinary passkey login on the unidentified form is regressed: the browser conditional UI has no WebAuthn parameters and cannot complete.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative cursor offsets are sliced and Django rejects them

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set (the audit-log endpoint always passes True), slices the queryset with a negative start if cursor.offset < 0. Django QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported for any negative start or stop; it does not emit a reverse OFFSET/LIMIT or "handle boundary conditions." Cursor.from_string already accepts a negative offset integer, so an otherwise authorized optimized_pagination request with a crafted or generated cursor 500s. The comment that this is safe because permissions are checked on the queryset is also wrong: the slice never runs, and a negative index would not be an authorization boundary anyway.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Optimized paginator cannot sort or cursor datetime audit rows

When optimized_pagination=true, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime". That class implements get_item_key/value_from_cursor like the integer Paginator: it math.floor/math.ceil's the raw field and feeds the cursor number straight back into the SQL comparison. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first page that has rows raises TypeError inside get_item_key while building the next/prev cursor, and a later page would compare a numeric cursor value to a timestamp column. DateTimePaginator already exists for this endpoint and converts timestamps correctly; this path does not, so the new admin pagination option 500s instead of paging audit logs.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

false_positives.candidate:
BasePaginator now silently clamps negative forward offsets for every endpoint

The shared BasePaginator.get_result path (used by Paginator and DateTimePaginator across the API, not only audit logs) now sets start_offset = max(0, offset) whenever the cursor is not a previous-page cursor, then slices from there. A forward cursor whose offset is negative used to fail closed on the queryset slice; it now returns the first page and still builds Link cursors as if that page were valid. Previous-page cursors still pass a negative offset through unchanged, so the same negative-index ValueError remains on is_prev. This is not a performance optimization and changes pagination failure behavior globally with no tests.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative cursor offsets passed into queryset slicing

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, uses the client-supplied cursor offset as the slice start (queryset[start_offset:stop]) and the comments say this is meant to reach rows beyond normal pagination bounds. Cursor.from_string already parses a negative offset with no check. Django querysets raise ValueError on negative slices, so this 500s; it does not implement reverse paging. BasePaginator was also changed so previous-page cursors keep a raw (possibly negative) offset on every endpoint that uses it. Negative offsets are not a safe or correct pagination mechanism here.

true_positives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Audit logs wired to a numeric paginator for a datetime column

When optimized_pagination=true, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint paginates AuditLogEntry with OptimizedCursorPaginator and order_by="-datetime". That class's get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, key) and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer. DateTimePaginator was the previous implementation because a datetime cannot be floored and the SQL bound must be a timezone-aware datetime, not an int. This path therefore raises TypeError while building the next cursor, or compares the datetime column to an integer, so any org owner or superuser who passes the query flag gets a 500 (or a wrong page) instead of audit logs.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

false_positives.candidate:
Hardcoded eviction drops spans with no metric or config

After merge, if the zset has more than 1000 members the script ZPOPMINs span_count-1000 members (lowest end_timestamp_precise) and returns success. The Python max_segment_spans limit (1001) and the flush-time segment_span_count_exceeded metric/error log were removed, and the cap is not passed into the script. The consumer will commit offsets for spans that were just deleted, with no signal that data was dropped, and the cap cannot be tuned via SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans. Eviction also runs on a span_count that stays 0-initialized unless a union happened, falling back to ZCARD only in that case; a union result that does not reflect members added only on the other key can under-count and leave the segment over the cap, or the next insert will delete the oldest payload including a root span while the has-root flag remains set.

Redirect walk cap cut from 10000 to 1000

The parent-redirect loop now stops at 1000 hops and the comment that this cap can fail to join deep segment trees was removed. On exit, the script still HSETs span_id to whatever set_span_id it stopped on and merges only that key. Traces whose redirect chain is deeper than 1000 are stored as split segments and later flushed with the wrong segment id, which the previous 10000 cap was explicitly there to avoid.

Set keys switched to sorted sets with no migration

add-buffer.lua and SpansBuffer now call ZCARD, ZUNIONSTORE, ZADD, ZSCAN, and ZPOPMIN on span-buf:s:* keys that existing consumers created with SADD/SUNIONSTORE. Redis returns WRONGTYPE if a key is still a set. During a rolling deploy, and for up to redis_ttl (default 3600s) after, insert and flush of in-flight segments fail, so spans are not buffered or cannot be flushed. There is no DEL/MIGRATE of old set keys and no WRONGTYPE handling.

ZUNIONSTORE sums scores and can double them

zunionstore is called without AGGREGATE MIN or MAX, so Redis's default SUM applies. When the same payload is already in both the destination segment key and the key being merged (retry, or span_key equal to set_key), the end_timestamp_precise score is added to itself. Eviction uses ZPOPMIN on those scores, so the wrong spans are dropped and ordering no longer matches end timestamps. The call should aggregate with MIN or MAX so a member keeps a single timestamp.

enable_advanced_features is not a paginate() argument

The new branch calls self.paginate(..., enable_advanced_features=True). Endpoint.paginate does not accept that keyword and does not forward arbitrary kwargs into the paginator constructor. The call either raises TypeError immediately or silently drops the flag, so OptimizedCursorPaginator.enable_advanced_features stays false and the branch that was supposed to change pagination never runs. The feature is also gated only by request.user.is_superuser or member.has_global_access, which is ordinary org-owner access, plus a client-controlled query param, on an unrelated spans-buffer change.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Eligibility cache key uses salted hash()

The cache key is built with hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's hash is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so each worker writes and reads a different key, and invalidate_upsampling_cache cannot delete keys other workers stored. The 60s cache does not dedupe option lookups across the fleet, and a hash collision could reuse another project set's allowlist decision. Nothing in this change calls the invalidator when the allowlist option changes, so a stable key would still be stale for up to 60s.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling decision ignores the query actually executed

_get_event_stats decides upsampling from the closed-over dataset and request.GET query, not from scoped_dataset or the query argument it is about to run. Dashboard discover-split rewrites that argument (for example to event.type:transaction or !event.type:transaction) and sometimes switches the dataset, but the count() -> upsampled_count() rewrite still follows the original request. Transaction or mixed queries can then sum sample_weight (missing or meaningless on those events), and error-only split queries can skip upsampling even when every project is allowlisted. Counts are wrong or the Snuba query fails.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

false_positives.candidate:
Error-query check is a substring match

_is_error_focused_query treats any query whose lowercased text contains "event.type:error" as error-only. That matches the negation !event.type:error, event.type:error.unhandled-style tokens, and the same text inside a quoted string or OR branch that also selects transactions. Discover queries that are not purely errors then get count() rewritten to sum(sample_weight), which mis-counts or errors on events that do not have that column.

Upsampled count sums sample_weight, but tests only set sample_rate

upsampled_count is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). The new store_event hook writes contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate into sample_rate (0.1 for a 10x sample) after manager.get_data(), and never sets sample_weight to 1/sample_rate. If weight was already derived, this mutation is too late; if Snuba reads sample_weight, the aggregate stays ~1 (or 0 if the column is null) while the new stats test expects 10. toInt64 also truncates fractional weights, so partial samples under-count even when the column is populated.

errors dataset rewrites count() to an undefined function

_should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True for the errors dataset, and the stats endpoint then replaces count() with upsampled_count(). That function is only registered on the discover dataset function converter. Errors-dataset timeseries requests for allowlisted projects will fail column/function resolution instead of returning an upsampled count.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error events are paired by dict value order, not node id

`fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, then zips `error_ids` with `nodestore.backend.get_multi(...).values()`. Dict iteration order is not guaranteed to match the input id list, so an error can be labeled with another event's id, title, and message in the Seer log. Look up each payload by its generated node id instead of zipping `.values()`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feature flag renders dashboard tables with empty data

When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `tableResultComponent` ignores the fetched `result` and renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and `tableData` hard-coded to empty `data`/`meta`. Every table widget behind that flag shows a blank table instead of the query results, field aliases, and custom renderers that the old chart still uses.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
60s deadline is too short for a 100-identity refresh batch

`check_auth_identities` walks up to `chunk_size` (100) identities and calls `provider.refresh_identity` (external IdP HTTP) for each, but `processing_deadline_duration` is 60 seconds. A slow batch is killed mid-loop; `last_synced` was already advanced in `check_auth`, so those identities are skipped until the next interval, and a retry can overlap with identities already refreshed in the same chunk.

Error timestamps from nodestore are compared as if they were floats

Event node `timestamp` is typically an ISO-8601 string, but `ErrorEvent` types it as `float` and `gen_request_data` compares it with `<` against breadcrumb timestamps (numbers). A string/float comparison raises TypeError outside the try/except in `fetch_error_details`, so any replay that has linked errors fails the summarize endpoint with 500 instead of producing a summary.

Hidden span attributes are only filtered while searching

`HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is applied only inside the search branch. When `searchQuery` is empty the function returns the full sorted list, so those fields stay visible in the default attributes tree—the opposite of hiding them—and disappear only after the user types a query.

PR comment helpers are on the wrong class and call a missing method

`get_environment_info` and `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` were added to `CommitContextIntegration`, but GitHub/GitLab call them as `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` / `self.get_environment_info` on `PRCommentWorkflow` subclasses, which do not inherit those methods. The static helper also calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title`, while `_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration`. Posting a merged-PR suspect-issue comment will raise AttributeError before a comment is sent.

Saved-search conversion migrations are no-ops with no replacement in this PR

Both 0917 and 0920 now return immediately and their tests were deleted. The comments point at `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`, which is not part of this change. Environments that have not already applied the old data migration will never copy organization saved searches into `GroupSearchView`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup codes are compared case-sensitively

Codes are generated with crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex"), which is lowercase, and both login and the disable endpoint match with indexOf after only stripping dashes. The input placeholder is "XXXXX-XXXXX", so users will type uppercase. Those codes will be rejected as incorrect even when they are valid, so backup-code login and 2FA disable via backup code fail for normal input. Normalize with toLowerCase() (and trim) before comparing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code plus any totpCode skips password

Password is verified only when credentials.totpCode is absent (the condition just above this branch). The new backup-code branch then runs whenever credentials.backupCode is set, and it never checks the password. A request that includes a valid backup code and any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000") therefore authenticates with no password at all. Backup codes are meant to replace the authenticator factor, not the password; the login UI still submits the password. Anyone who obtains a backup code (screenshot, downloaded file, clipboard) can mint a session without knowing the account password.

Codes are shown only after 2FA is already on, and dismiss loses them

handleEnable persists twoFactorEnabled on the server and only then switches to DisplayBackupCodes. onEnable (and thus the parent updating the security page) runs solely from the Close button. Dialog onOpenChange is not intercepted, and resetState does not clear or revoke the codes. Closing the dialog, refreshing, or navigating away after a successful enable leaves 2FA on with the only plaintext copy of the codes discarded and no regenerate API. The user can be locked out of their authenticator recovery path.

Download control cannot download the codes

The download link wraps a Button that sits inside the enable Form and has no type="button" and no preventDefault. A button defaults to type="submit", so the click submits handleEnable again instead of activating the parent anchor, and a button nested in an <a> does not reliably start the download. Users who just enabled 2FA can be left without a saved copy of codes that are never shown again.

Enable-and-login e2e never leaves the backup-code step

After a correct OTP, enable now stays on the backup-code screen and does not call onEnable until backup-codes-close is clicked. This test never clicks that button (unlike the disable test) and immediately waits for the two-factor switch. The switch state is updated only in onEnable, and the modal is still open, so this test no longer completes a real enable. The new FIXME also admits the isChecked assertion passes even when the switch is unchecked, so the suite will not catch the broken flow.

Lost access button submits the disable form

The new Lost access / Go back button is inside Form and has no type="button". HTML buttons default to submit, so clicking it both toggles the backup-code view and posts handleDisable with whatever totp/backup values are currently registered. That can disable 2FA unintentionally or surface a spurious incorrect-code error while switching modes. Cancel has the same default and should be type="button" as well.

Password visibility toggle is overridden

PasswordField sets type from isPasswordVisible and then spreads {...props}. This call passes type="password", which overwrites that value, so the show/hide control added by switching this field to PasswordField never reveals the password.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty

The Meet-without-Google-Calendar fallback now destructures the first destination calendar and reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration with no null check. destinationCalendar is often null or [] (no calendar connected, or the new array conversion produced an empty list). That throws TypeError before the booking is created, so a Google Meet event type with no destination calendar fails entirely instead of falling back to Cal Video. The previous optional chain (destinationCalendar?.integration) did not throw.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update/delete fallback search can never match a calendar

When externalCalendarId is missing, updateEvent and deleteEvent do destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId). The right-hand side is null/undefined/empty, so the find never matches a real calendar id. Previously this path used destinationCalendar.externalId. Updates and deletes for bookings that have no stored externalCalendarId now hit an undefined calendarId (update) or silently fall back to "primary" (delete), so the event on the chosen calendar is not updated or removed. The hangout-link patch in createEvent has the same problem: it passes selectedCalendar without the || "primary" used by insert.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug condition was inverted

The org create payload changed from spreading slug when team billing is disabled (!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }) to spreading slug only when billing is enabled. requestedSlug is still set when billing is enabled. With billing off, the new organization is created with no slug, so the org URL is never registered. With billing on, both slug and requestedSlug are set, which is the opposite of the previous split. This is unrelated to destination calendars and looks like an accidental boolean flip.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Office 365 always writes the first destination calendar

createEvent still takes only the first element of destinationCalendar and ignores the credentialId that CalendarManager now passes. EventManager loops every collective host and calls createEvent with the full array plus that host's credential. Office 365 therefore creates every host's event on the first host's calendar (or the default calendar) and never on the other hosts' calendars. The same first-element-only pattern is in Lark (create/update/delete) and CalDAV, so non-Google collective hosts are not actually invited on their own calendars.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent is called when credential is still missing

After the in-memory lookup and the DB fetch, updateAllCalendarEvents still pushes updateEvent(credential, ...) even if credential is undefined (no row, or app.slug missing so the fetch result is discarded). CalendarManager then calls getCalendar(undefined), the throw is caught, and every calendar reference in the batch is reported as failed. A single missing credential aborts updates for the other hosts instead of skipping that reference.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

false_positives.candidate:
Collective host calendars dropped when organizer has none

For collective events, other hosts' destination calendars are appended with evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). The array is initialized to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, so optional chaining skips the push. Those hosts never get a calendar event, which is exactly the case this PR is meant to fix. Initialize an array before pushing, including when the organizer has no calendar.

Google organizer email is always the first host's calendar

createEvent and updateEvent set the organizer attendee email from destinationCalendar[0].externalId, while the calendar written to is chosen by credentialId. For a collective booking each host's Google credential receives the same event, so secondary hosts' events list the first host's calendar id as organizer. Google can reject the insert, or the wrong person is marked organizer and the real host is only a guest. Use the destination entry whose credentialId matches the credential creating the event.

Recurring cancel deletes only the first calendar reference, with every credential

Inside the per-reference loop, cancelling all remaining recurring instances ignores the current reference and instead walks every user calendar credential, and for each updated booking only bookingRef = references.find(_calendar). Collective bookings now store one calendar reference per host, so only the first host's event is targeted, and it is deleted once per calendar credential (duplicate/wrong-credential deletes). Other hosts' recurring events are left on their calendars. Delete each updated booking's calendar references with the credential stored on that reference, as the non-recurring branch does.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync-mode token schema cannot accept a real token response

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()], which are the literal property names "ZodString" and "ZodOptional", not a catchall. Zod object schemas also strip unknown keys. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, safeParse requires a numeric "ZodString" field and rejects normal { access_token, expires_in } bodies, so every synced refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". The same function then, if refresh_token is absent, writes the literal string "refresh_token" onto the parsed data (line 26), which callers persist and use for the next refresh, permanently invalidating the grant.

Google refresh persists the Zod result object instead of the tokens

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync refresh returns an unparsed, unauthenticated fetch Response

When credential sync is on, refreshOAuthTokens POSTs only calcomUserId and appSlug as form fields and returns the raw fetch Response. There is no shared secret or other authenticator, so the parent app cannot tell this call from an anonymous request, and Cal.com will treat whatever body comes back as tokens. Callers are also not updated for this shape: Google reads res.data, HubSpot treats the return value as a HubspotToken, and Zoho Bigin/CRM read axios .data. Those paths throw or store undefined tokens whenever sync is enabled. The Zoom caller also passes app slug "zoomvideo" while credentials are stored as appId "zoom", so a sync lookup by slug will miss the app.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Credential webhook accepts any method and writes unvalidated decrypted JSON

The handler never checks req.method, and appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse is not caught, so a bad body becomes an unhandled 500. After a successful secret check it JSON.parses the decrypted string and writes that value straight into credential.key (create or update) with no schema for the app. A sync sender bug, or anyone who has the webhook secret, can replace a user's OAuth credential with arbitrary JSON. findFirst-then-create is also not transactional, so concurrent deliveries can insert duplicate credentials for the same user and app, and later findFirst updates will only touch one of them.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

false_positives.candidate:
OAuth helper imports decodeOAuthState from a path that does not exist

After the move into _utils/oauth, createOAuthAppCredential imports decodeOAuthState from "../oauth/decodeOAuthState". That resolves to _utils/oauth/oauth/decodeOAuthState, which is not a file.
